story.iWant: to create a new customer via REST API
story.soThat: I can add new customers to the system
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create CustomerController with POST endpoint (AC: #1, #9) - Task 2: Create CustomerService with create business logic (AC: #2, #3, #7, #8) - Task 3: Create request/response DTOs (AC: #2, #3) - Task 4: Implement duplicate email detection and conflict handling (AC: #5) - Task 5: Implement request/response structured JSON logging (AC: #6) - Task 6: Implement automatic audit entry creation (AC: #7) - Task 7: Implement authorization checks (AC: #9) - Task 8: Performance testing and optimization (AC: #10) - Task 9: Implement error handling and validation (AC: #4) - Task 10: Integration tests for full API flow (AC: #1-10) - Task 11: Documentation and API contract (AC: #1-3)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. POST /api/v1/customers endpoint implemented with @PostMapping("/customers") 2. Request body schema accepts: firstName, lastName, dateOfBirth, email, phone, address, city, state, zipCode 3. Returns 201 Created with response body containing: customerId, firstName, lastName, email, phone, status, createdAt, plus metadata (timestamp, version) 4. Validation errors return 400 Bad Request with field-level errors 5. Duplicate email returns 409 Conflict with message: "Customer with this email already exists" 6. Request/response logged in structured JSON format (info level) 7. Audit entry created automatically (operation: CREATE, user from JWT token, all field values) 8. Default status set to ACTIVE 9. Requires ROLE_CUSTOMER_SERVICE_AGENT or higher authorization 10. Response time < 200ms typical

doc.title: CICS GenApp Cloud Modernization - Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: FR001: Add customer record with required personal/contact information (COBOL: SSC1 transaction equivalent). FR013: Audit logging for all data mutations (who, what, when, why, before/after values). FR019: Role-based access control (RBAC: customer service agents, admin).

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Modern system uses Spring MVC controllers for REST endpoints, service layer for business logic, and repository layer for data access. Replaces COBOL SSC1 transaction with POST /api/v1/customers endpoint.

doc.title: Story 2.1: Customer Domain Model and PostgreSQL Schema
doc.snippet: Story 2.1 provides Customer JPA entity with validation annotations and CustomerRepository with findByEmail() method. This story uses these for persistence and email uniqueness checking.

doc.title: Story 1.2: Spring Boot Starter Project with Core Configuration
doc.snippet: Story 1.2 established GlobalExceptionHandler with @ControllerAdvice for centralized error handling. This story extends it to handle validation errors, duplicate key exceptions, and business exceptions.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Epic 2: Customer Service API & Spring Boot Backend
doc.snippet: Story 2.2 implements first REST API endpoint (POST /api/v1/customers) for customer creation, replacing legacy COBOL SSC1 transaction. Sets pattern for subsequent CRUD operations (Stories 2.3-2.6).

artifact.reason: Existing exception handler. Extend to handle MethodArgumentNotValidException (400), DuplicateKeyException (409), and business exceptions.
Existing exception class. Pattern for creating CustomerAlreadyExistsException for duplicate email handling.
Existing exception class for duplicate key violations. Use for email uniqueness constraint failures.
Existing security configuration. Ensures @PreAuthorize annotations are processed and JWT tokens provide role information.
Existing logging filter. May be used or extended for request/response JSON logging with MDC trace ID.
Existing controller example. Pattern for creating CustomerController with REST endpoints, @RestController, and ResponseEntity.

story-context.constraints: - Java 21 LTS required (established in Story 1.1) - Spring Boot 3.3.4 LTS (established in Story 1.2) - REST API endpoint pattern: POST /api/v1/customers (API versioning required) - Authorization: Requires ROLE_CUSTOMER_SERVICE_AGENT or ROLE_ADMIN (enforced via @PreAuthorize) - Email uniqueness: Business rule enforced (check before save, return 409 if exists) - Default status: ACTIVE (set in service layer before persisting) - Response time: < 200ms typical (performance requirement) - Audit trail: Automatic audit entry creation for all CREATE operations - Structured logging: JSON format with trace ID, user ID, timestamp - Error handling: Field-level validation errors returned as 400 with detailed messages - Request/Response DTOs: Separate from entity model (CreateCustomerRequest, CustomerResponse) - Service layer pattern: Controller delegates to CustomerService for business logic - HTTP status codes: 201 Created (success), 400 Bad Request (validation), 409 Conflict (duplicate), 403 Forbidden (unauthorized) - Package structure: controller/, service/, dto/ packages under com.example.cicsgenapp - Google Java Style Guide (Checkstyle enforced) - Story 2.1 must be completed first (Customer entity and repository required)

tests.standards: Testing standards for Story 2.2 require 85%+ test coverage for controller and service classes. Use JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test, MockMvc for controller testing, and Mockito for service layer unit tests. Integration tests use @SpringBootTest with Testcontainers for PostgreSQL. API contract tests verify request/response schema. Performance tests verify <200ms response time. Error path tests cover validation errors, duplicate email, unauthorized access.

tests.ideas: AC1: Controller test - POST /api/v1/customers with valid data, verify 201 status and endpoint mapping works AC2: DTO validation test - Verify CreateCustomerRequest accepts all fields (firstName, lastName, dateOfBirth, email, phone, address, city, state, zipCode) AC3: Controller test - Verify 201 response contains customerId, firstName, lastName, email, phone, status, createdAt, and metadata (timestamp, version) AC4: Controller test - POST with invalid email format, verify 400 Bad Request with field-level error details AC5: Service test - Call createCustomer() with duplicate email, verify CustomerAlreadyExistsException thrown; Controller test - verify 409 Conflict response AC6: Integration test - POST customer, verify request and response logged in JSON format with trace ID AC7: Service test - Verify auditService.createAuditEntry() called with operation=CREATE, user from JWT token, all customer field values AC8: Service test - Verify default status set to ACTIVE when creating customer AC9: Controller test - POST without CUSTOMER_SERVICE_AGENT role, verify 403 Forbidden response AC10: Performance test - POST 1000+ requests, verify P99 response time < 200ms
